title: Domain 2 extra questions (2.1-2.5)
note: Original questions written for IdentityOps Lab. Not from exam dumps or commercial banks.

questions.stem: A threat intelligence report describes a group with managers, recruiters and paid developers. It runs phishing campaigns, sells stolen card numbers on dark web markets and launders the proceeds through cryptocurrency mixers. Which of the following threat actors BEST fits this description?
questions.explanation: A business-like structure focused on turning stolen data into money is typical of organized crime. A nation-state is also well organized, but its goals are usually espionage or strategic advantage rather than selling card numbers.

questions.stem: A threat report uses the term advanced persistent threat (APT) to describe a group that has kept hidden access to several government networks for years. Which of the following threat actors is this term MOST commonly associated with?
questions.explanation: APT describes long-term, stealthy, well-resourced campaigns, which is the hallmark of nation-state actors. Hacktivists may be persistent, but they usually seek publicity rather than years of quiet access.

questions.stem: A town's library website was knocked offline for an afternoon. Police traced the attack to a teenager in another state who had downloaded a ready-made flooding script from a video tutorial and admitted he did not know how it worked. Which of the following BEST describes this threat actor?
questions.explanation: Someone who runs downloaded tools without understanding them is an unskilled attacker. A hacktivist would act for a stated cause, and nothing in the scenario suggests one.

questions.stem: A group named after an animal rights cause broke into a cosmetics company's web server and posted the company's internal product-testing reports online along with a manifesto. Which of the following threat actors is MOST likely responsible?
questions.explanation: Publishing data with a manifesto to promote a cause is classic hacktivism. Organized crime would try to profit from the data, for example by selling it or demanding a ransom, rather than releasing it for free.

questions.stem: To speed up testing, a developer set up a personal cloud server without telling IT and copied part of the production customer database to it. The developer meant no harm. Which of the following BEST describes this situation?
questions.explanation: Shadow IT is technology used for work without the approval or knowledge of the IT department, usually with good intentions. The developer is not trying to profit or promote a cause, so organized crime and hacktivist do not fit.

questions.stem: A database administrator who was passed over for promotion copied the full customer list to a personal USB drive the week before resigning to join a competitor. Which of the following threat actors BEST describes the administrator?
questions.explanation: An employee who abuses authorized access to steal data is an insider threat. Shadow IT describes well-meaning use of unapproved technology, not deliberate theft.

questions.stem: While sending a report, an HR assistant let the email client autocomplete the wrong recipient, and a spreadsheet of employee tax IDs went to an outside address. The assistant reported the mistake right away. Which of the following BEST describes this threat?
questions.explanation: An insider who causes harm through a mistake, with no intent to do so, is an unintentional insider threat. A malicious insider acts on purpose, and nothing here suggests that.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the main security problem created by shadow IT?
choices: The systems are not managed or monitored by the security team
The systems must run only open-source software
The users usually intend to sell company data to competitors for profit
The systems are always controlled by outside attackers
questions.answer: The systems are not managed or monitored by the security team
questions.explanation: Because shadow IT is set up without IT's knowledge, it misses patching, monitoring and security review. Its users are usually well-meaning, so profit-driven intent is not the defining problem.

questions.stem: A sales team started using a free browser extension that records and transcribes customer calls. Nobody asked IT, and the extension uploads every recording to the vendor's servers. Which of the following BEST describes this threat?
questions.explanation: Staff adopting an unapproved tool that handles company data is shadow IT. No outside group is attacking the company, so nation-state and organized crime do not apply.

questions.stem: A call center agent was paid by an outside group to look up customer accounts and photograph the details on screen. Which of the following BEST describes the agent?
questions.explanation: The agent uses legitimate internal access to steal data, which makes the agent an insider threat. The outside group paying the agent may be organized crime, but the question asks about the agent.

questions.stem: When classifying threat actors, which of the following attributes describes whether the actor already has access inside the organization?
questions.explanation: The internal/external attribute separates actors who already have inside access, such as employees, from those attacking from outside. Sophistication describes skill, not where the actor starts.

questions.stem: After an incident, analysts found that the attacker wrote custom malware, used encrypted command channels and wiped its own traces with anti-forensics tools. Which of the following threat actor attributes does this evidence MOST directly show?
questions.explanation: Custom tools and careful anti-forensics show a high level of skill and capability. Funding may support such skill, but the evidence itself measures what the attacker can do, not how much money it has.

questions.stem: A criminal group rents thousands of cloud servers, buys initial access to victim networks from brokers and pays affiliates a share of every ransom. Which of the following threat actor attributes is MOST evident?
questions.explanation: Renting large infrastructure and buying access shows that the group has significant money to spend. Nothing in the scenario describes the group's own technical skill, so sophistication is not the best answer.

questions.stem: A contractor with a valid badge and network account plugged a hardware keylogger into a manager's workstation. Why are perimeter firewalls LEAST effective against this type of threat actor?
choices: The actor always has the funding of a nation-state government
The actor is driven by political beliefs
The actor is already inside with authorized access
The actor only uses zero-day exploits
questions.answer: The actor is already inside with authorized access
questions.explanation: Perimeter defenses filter traffic coming from outside, but an internal actor already has legitimate access past them. Insiders are not defined by funding, zero-days or politics.

questions.stem: Which of the following threat actors is typically rated LOWEST in both resources and sophistication?
questions.explanation: An unskilled attacker usually works alone with free tools and little money. Hacktivist groups vary, but they often include skilled members and can pool resources for a cause.

questions.stem: An attacker installed cryptocurrency mining software on hundreds of a company's cloud servers. The company's compute bill tripled while the coins went to the attacker's wallet. Which of the following motivations BEST describes this attack?
questions.explanation: Using someone else's computing power to mine coins is done to make money. The servers kept running, so service disruption was a side effect rather than the goal.

questions.stem: Which of the following motivations describes an attacker whose main goal is to copy sensitive information out of an organization to a location the attacker controls?
questions.explanation: Data exfiltration is the unauthorized transfer of data out of an organization. Blackmail may follow a theft, but it is defined by the threat used to pressure the victim, not by the copying itself.

questions.stem: A group defaced dozens of unrelated websites, deleted files at random and posted that they did it to watch things break. They asked for no money and promoted no cause. Which of the following motivations is MOST likely?
questions.explanation: Random damage with no profit or message points to a desire for disruption and chaos. Political beliefs would come with a cause or message, which the group did not have.

questions.stem: Attackers repeatedly flooded a city's online emergency reporting system with traffic so residents could not submit reports. Nothing was stolen and no payment was demanded. Which of the following motivations BEST describes this attack?
questions.explanation: The goal was to stop a service from working, which is service disruption. No data left the system, so data exfiltration and espionage do not fit.

questions.stem: Employees at a design firm received direct messages in the company's chat platform from an external guest account. Each message contained a link to a shared project file that installed malware. Which of the following threat vectors was used?
questions.explanation: Messages sent through a chat or collaboration platform use the instant messaging vector. SMS refers to text messages sent over the mobile phone network, not to a workplace chat tool.

questions.stem: An attacker left voicemails for several employees claiming to be the bank's fraud department and asked them to call back a number the attacker controlled. Which of the following threat vectors does this BEST describe?
questions.explanation: The lure is delivered by phone and voicemail, which is the voice call vector. Email could carry a similar story, but nothing in this attack was sent by email.

questions.stem: A company is choosing between a remote support tool that needs a program installed on every laptop and one that runs entirely in a web browser. From an attack surface view, which of the following is the MAIN advantage of the browser-based option?
choices: It encrypts all data on the laptop's disk
It cannot be affected by any software vulnerability at all
It removes the need for user authentication
No extra client software on each laptop can be exploited
questions.answer: No extra client software on each laptop can be exploited
questions.explanation: Agentless tools avoid adding installed software to every endpoint, so there is less client-based code for attackers to exploit. They still have vulnerabilities on the server side, so they are not immune.

questions.stem: The payroll team still uses a desktop accounting program whose vendor went out of business four years ago. A flaw in the program's file import feature was published last week. Which of the following BEST explains why this program is a high-risk threat vector?
choices: It is unsupported and will not receive security fixes
It is exposed to the internet on an open service port
questions.answer: It is unsupported and will not receive security fixes
questions.explanation: Software with no vendor support stays vulnerable because no patch will ever be released. Nothing in the scenario mentions default logins or listening network ports.

questions.stem: An attacker exploited a flaw in an outdated browser plug-in that employees still had installed, even though no business task needed it anymore. Which of the following threat vectors was used?
questions.explanation: The flaw was in software installed on the users' devices, which is client-based vulnerable software. Open service ports refer to listening network services, not a browser plug-in.

questions.stem: A coffee shop's guest Wi-Fi uses no encryption. An attacker sitting in the shop captures other customers' unencrypted traffic as it passes over the air. Which of the following threat vectors is being exploited?
questions.explanation: An open Wi-Fi network lets anyone within range capture the traffic, which makes it an unsecure wireless vector. Nothing is plugged into a cable, so the wired vector does not apply.

questions.stem: At a trade show, an attacker sent unsolicited files to nearby phones and copied contact lists from several phones that were left discoverable and accepted pairing without a PIN. Which of the following threat vectors was used?
questions.explanation: Discoverable phones that pair without a PIN expose the Bluetooth vector, which allows attacks such as bluejacking and bluesnarfing. The attacker never joined a Wi-Fi network, so the wireless network vector is not the best fit.

questions.stem: A visitor plugged a laptop into an active network jack in a building lobby and received an address on the internal network with no authentication. Which of the following threat vectors does this BEST describe?
questions.explanation: A live network jack that grants access without authentication is an unsecure wired network. Open service ports refer to services listening on a host, not to physical network access.

questions.stem: A remote employee's home router still uses an old Wi-Fi encryption protocol that attackers can crack in minutes. Which of the following threat vectors does this create for the company laptop used there?
questions.explanation: Weak, crackable Wi-Fi encryption makes the wireless network itself an unsecure vector. Default credentials would concern the router's admin login, which the scenario does not mention.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST example of an unsecure wired network threat vector?
choices: A phone left discoverable to nearby devices
An attacker joining an open guest Wi-Fi network
A rogue device plugged into an open conference room jack
A fake access point broadcasting the company network name
questions.answer: A rogue device plugged into an open conference room jack
questions.explanation: Plugging into an unprotected Ethernet jack attacks the wired network. The fake access point and open guest Wi-Fi are wireless vectors, and the discoverable phone is a Bluetooth vector.

questions.stem: A new network-attached storage device was connected with SSH, FTP, SMB and a web interface all enabled, but staff only use SMB to reach their files. Which of the following attack surfaces does this BEST describe?
questions.explanation: Every enabled service listens on a port that attackers can probe, so unneeded services widen the attack surface. The scenario says nothing about factory logins, so default credentials is not the issue described.

questions.stem: Which of the following attack surfaces is MOST easily exploited using username and password lists collected from vendor manuals and support websites?
questions.explanation: Vendors publish factory usernames and passwords, so devices that keep them can be logged in to with public lists. Open ports expose services, but they do not by themselves give the attacker a working login.

questions.stem: A smart TV in the boardroom was found running a debug Telnet service that the manufacturer left enabled and that any device on the network can connect to. Which of the following attack surfaces does this BEST describe?
questions.explanation: A forgotten service listening for connections is an open service port that attackers can reach. Bluetooth and removable devices are separate vectors that do not involve a network listener.

questions.stem: A heating and cooling maintenance vendor had remote access to a retailer's network to monitor equipment. Attackers stole the vendor's credentials and used that access to reach the retailer's payment systems. Which of the following threat vectors does this BEST describe?
questions.explanation: The attackers reached the retailer through a trusted vendor's access, which is a supply chain vector. The vendor's credentials were stolen, not factory defaults, so default credentials does not fit.

questions.stem: A company bought network switches whose firmware contained a hidden administrator account that the supplier's subcontractor had inserted during manufacturing. Which of the following threat vectors BEST describes how the weakness entered the company?
questions.explanation: The weakness came in through a supplier before the devices ever arrived, which is a supply chain vector. A hidden account added on purpose is a backdoor, not a documented factory default.

questions.stem: Why does a managed service provider (MSP) represent a supply chain threat vector for its customers?
choices: Its trusted access to many customer networks can be abused
It always leaves default credentials on devices
It removes the customer's need for any internal security staff
It stores all customer data in public storage
questions.answer: Its trusted access to many customer networks can be abused
questions.explanation: An MSP holds privileged access to many customers at once, so compromising the MSP opens a path into all of them. MSPs do not inherently use default credentials; the risk comes from the trust and access they hold.

questions.stem: An employee shared a social media post claiming the company's VPN had been hacked and urging coworkers to stop using it. The employee believed the post was true, but it was false. Which of the following BEST describes the employee's post?
questions.explanation: Misinformation is false information spread by someone who believes it is true. Disinformation would require the person to know the claim is false and spread it on purpose.

questions.stem: A man in a high-visibility vest carrying a clipboard told the receptionist he worked for the electric company and needed to inspect the meter room. The receptionist let him in. Which of the following social engineering techniques did he use?
questions.explanation: Pretending to be a trusted worker to gain access is impersonation. Business email compromise uses a real or spoofed email account, and no email was involved here.

questions.stem: A product search page builds its database query directly from whatever the user types. When a tester enters a single apostrophe, the page shows a database syntax error. Which of the following vulnerabilities is MOST likely present?
questions.explanation: A database error triggered by a quote character shows that user input is changing the structure of the SQL query. Cross-site scripting affects scripts run in the browser, not database queries.

questions.stem: A site's search page displays No results for followed by the search term exactly as typed. A link with a script in the search term runs that script in the browser of anyone who clicks it. Which of the following vulnerabilities is present?
questions.explanation: Reflecting unencoded input back into a page lets attacker script run in the victim's browser, which is cross-site scripting. SQL injection targets the database, and nothing here reaches a database.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the root cause shared by SQL injection and cross-site scripting vulnerabilities?
choices: The application stores passwords in plain text
The web server's operating system has passed its vendor end-of-life date
The server uses an outdated encryption cipher
The application trusts input without validating or encoding it
questions.answer: The application trusts input without validating or encoding it
questions.explanation: Both flaws exist because untrusted input is passed into a query or a page without proper validation or encoding. Weak ciphers and plaintext passwords are cryptographic issues, not injection issues.

questions.stem: A newly announced flaw in a built-in Windows service lets any local user gain full system privileges on every unpatched workstation, no matter which applications are installed. Which of the following types of vulnerabilities is this?
questions.explanation: The flaw lives in a component of the operating system itself, so it affects every unpatched machine. An application vulnerability would depend on a particular program being installed.

questions.stem: A factory's production line is controlled by a computer running a 20-year-old operating system. The vendor still sells paid extended support, but the computer cannot run modern security agents. Which of the following BEST describes this system?
questions.explanation: A legacy system is old and outdated but may still be in use and even receive limited support. Nothing points to a flaw in low-level device code, so firmware is not the best description of the system as a whole.

questions.stem: A laptop maker released a BIOS update to fix a flaw that let attackers turn off secure boot before the operating system loads. Which of the following types of vulnerabilities did the update fix?
questions.explanation: The BIOS is firmware stored on the motherboard, so a flaw in it is a firmware vulnerability. It runs before the operating system starts, which is why it is not an operating system flaw.

questions.stem: A security team learns that the hypervisor on its virtualization cluster has a flaw that lets code in a guest run on the host. Why is this vulnerability MORE serious than a similar flaw on a single physical server?
choices: One compromise can affect every guest on that host
Virtual machines cannot receive security patches from their vendors
questions.answer: One compromise can affect every guest on that host
questions.explanation: Breaking out to the host exposes all the virtual machines that share it, so the impact is multiplied. Virtual machines can be patched and encrypted, so those distractors are false.

questions.stem: Which of the following categories of vulnerabilities BEST describes weaknesses such as insecure provider APIs, weak tenant isolation and exposed management consoles?
questions.explanation: Provider APIs, tenant isolation and management consoles are features of cloud environments, so these are cloud-specific vulnerabilities. They do not depend on a particular operating system or device.

questions.stem: When a virtual desktop session ends, the pool hands the same virtual disk to the next user without resetting it. The next user finds the previous user's downloaded files. Which of the following vulnerabilities does this describe?
questions.explanation: Reassigning storage to a new user without clearing it is resource reuse. VM escape involves breaking out of a guest to reach the host, which did not happen here.

questions.stem: Attackers compromised the maintainer of a third-party JavaScript library and published a tampered release, which a retailer then included in its checkout pages. Every checkout page began sending card details to the attackers. Which of the following supply chain risks does this represent?
questions.explanation: The compromised component is code supplied by a third party, which is a software provider risk. No physical device was tampered with, so the hardware provider risk does not apply.

questions.stem: A company outsourced its help desk. Attackers compromised the outsourcing firm and used its staff accounts to reset passwords for the company's employees. Which of the following supply chain risks does this represent?
questions.explanation: The weakness came from a third party providing a service with access to company systems. No code or devices from the vendor were involved, so software and hardware provider risks do not fit.

questions.stem: Which of the following practices BEST reduces supply chain risk from hardware providers?
choices: Scanning every internal web application for injection flaws before release
Requiring longer passwords for all users
Moving all servers to a public cloud
Buying only through authorized channels and checking device integrity
questions.answer: Buying only through authorized channels and checking device integrity
questions.explanation: Counterfeit or tampered hardware usually enters through unauthorized resellers, so buying from trusted channels and verifying devices reduces the risk. Moving to the cloud just shifts the hardware risk to another provider.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST example of a software provider supply chain risk?
choices: A vulnerable open-source library inside a purchased app
A server delivered with a damaged power supply
An outsourced help desk with weak reset procedures
A counterfeit network card from a gray-market reseller
questions.answer: A vulnerable open-source library inside a purchased app
questions.explanation: A flawed component built into software from a vendor is a software provider risk. The counterfeit network card is a hardware provider risk, and the help desk is a service provider risk.

questions.stem: A code review finds that a web application stores user passwords as unsalted MD5 hashes. Which of the following types of vulnerabilities is this?
questions.explanation: MD5 is a weak hash, and without salts identical passwords produce identical hashes, so the protection is easy to break. This is a cryptographic weakness, not a memory or mobile flaw.

questions.stem: A new web server went live with directory listing turned on and the vendor's sample applications still installed. Which of the following vulnerabilities is MOST likely?
questions.explanation: Leaving insecure defaults and sample content in place is a misconfiguration. A zero-day is an unknown flaw with no patch, while this problem can be fixed simply by changing settings.

questions.stem: While troubleshooting, an administrator added a firewall rule that allows all traffic from any source to any destination and forgot to remove it. Which of the following vulnerabilities did this create?
questions.explanation: An overly permissive rule left in place by mistake is a misconfiguration. The firewall's software and firmware are working as designed, so it is not a firmware flaw.

questions.stem: Why do organizations commonly block side loading on company-managed phones?
choices: Side loading switches off the cellular radio
Side-loaded apps cannot ever be uninstalled
Side loading always requires jailbreaking or rooting the device first
Apps from outside the official store skip its security review
questions.answer: Apps from outside the official store skip its security review
questions.explanation: Official app stores screen apps before publishing them, and side-loaded apps bypass that review. Many devices can side load without being jailbroken, so the jailbreaking option is false.

questions.stem: Attackers began exploiting a flaw in a popular email server on the same day it was discovered, before the vendor had published any advisory or patch. Which of the following BEST describes this vulnerability?
questions.explanation: A flaw exploited before the vendor knows about it or can fix it is a zero-day. An end-of-life product may go unpatched because the vendor is ending support, not because the flaw is new.

questions.stem: A free browser toolbar that a user installed quietly records every website visited and every search term entered, then sends the data to a marketing server. Which of the following types of malware is this?
questions.explanation: Software that secretly collects information about a user's activity and sends it elsewhere is spyware. A worm spreads on its own across a network, which the toolbar does not do.

questions.stem: A shipment of new laptops arrived with many vendor trial programs and utilities already installed. They slow the laptops down, are not needed and are rarely updated. Which of the following BEST describes this software?
questions.explanation: Unneeded software preinstalled by the manufacturer is bloatware; it wastes resources and adds unpatched attack surface. A trojan pretends to be useful in order to deliver hidden malicious code, which is not described here.

questions.stem: Malicious code attached itself to program files on a shared drive. It spread only when users ran one of the infected programs and then infected other programs on their computers. Which of the following types of malware is this?
questions.explanation: A virus attaches to other files and needs a user to run the infected file to spread. A worm spreads by itself across the network without any user action.

questions.stem: Overnight, someone pried open a locked side door of a data center and broke the lock on a server rack to remove several drives. Which of the following attacks does this BEST describe?
questions.explanation: Forcing doors and locks open is a physical brute force attack. Tailgating means following an authorized person through a door, and no one was present here.

questions.stem: An intruder held a heat source to a sensor in a server room, which set off the fire suppression system and forced an emergency shutdown of every server. Which of the following types of attacks is this?
questions.explanation: Manipulating building systems such as fire suppression, power or cooling to disrupt computers is an environmental attack. The intruder did not force any lock or barrier, so it is not physical brute force.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST indicator that an employee's access badge may have been cloned?
choices: The photo printed on the badge has faded
The badge opened doors in two buildings at the same moment
The main entrance badge reader went offline
The employee was issued a temporary badge after forgetting it one day
questions.answer: The badge opened doors in two buildings at the same moment
questions.explanation: A single badge cannot be in two places at once, so simultaneous use strongly suggests a copy exists. A temporary badge is a normal process and does not show that the original was copied.

questions.stem: A company's server is receiving a flood of SYN-ACK packets from hundreds of legitimate web servers, even though it never sent them any connection requests. Each reply is about the same size as the request that caused it. Which of the following attacks is MOST likely taking place?
questions.explanation: The attacker spoofs the victim's address so that third-party servers reflect their replies at it, which is a reflected DDoS. It is not amplified because the replies are no larger than the requests.

questions.stem: Laptops on the office Wi-Fi keep dropping their connections. A wireless capture shows a stream of management frames ordering clients to disconnect that appear to come from the company's access point but are sent by an unknown device. Which of the following attacks is MOST likely occurring?
questions.explanation: Forged deauthentication frames knock clients off the wireless network. This is often done before an evil twin attack, but the capture shows no fake access point, only the forced disconnections.

questions.stem: An attacker captured a valid sign-in request on the network and later sent it to the application again without changing it. The application accepted it and opened a session for the attacker. Which of the following attacks is this?
questions.explanation: Resending captured valid data to gain access is a replay attack. Brute force involves guessing many passwords, but the attacker here guessed nothing.

questions.stem: A web application firewall logs the following request to an order lookup page: `id=105; DROP TABLE orders--`. Which of the following attacks does this request show?
questions.explanation: The request adds a database command to an input field, which is a SQL injection attempt. Directory traversal would use ../ sequences to reach files outside the web folder.

questions.stem: A service's crash log shows that a client sent a username field containing 5,000 letter A characters followed by unreadable binary data, and then the service restarted unexpectedly. Which of the following attacks is MOST likely?
questions.explanation: An oversized input followed by binary data and a crash is a typical sign of a buffer overflow attempt to overwrite memory. Injection inserts commands into a query or interpreter rather than overrunning a memory buffer.

questions.stem: Researchers produced two different contract documents that have the same MD5 hash, so a digital signature on one also appears valid on the other. Which of the following attacks does this describe?
questions.explanation: A collision occurs when two different inputs produce the same hash, which defeats integrity checks and signatures. A downgrade attack forces weaker protocol settings and does not create matching hashes.

questions.stem: On hotel Wi-Fi, an on-path device stripped the redirect that normally moves visitors from the HTTP to the HTTPS version of a banking site, so the user's session stayed unencrypted. Which of the following attacks is this?
questions.explanation: Forcing a connection to use a weaker or unencrypted mode, as in SSL stripping, is a downgrade attack. Collision and birthday attacks target hash functions, not the choice of protocol.

questions.stem: A security architect replaced a short 64-bit hash used to check file integrity with SHA-256, specifically so attackers cannot practically find any two files with the same hash. Which of the following attacks is the architect MOST directly defending against?
questions.explanation: A birthday attack uses probability to find matching hashes in far fewer attempts than expected, and short hashes make that practical. Longer hash outputs defend against it; downgrade and replay attacks are unaffected by hash length.

questions.stem: An attacker stole a copy of a company's password hash database and is testing billions of guesses per second on their own hardware. No failed logins appear in the company's logs. Which of the following attacks is this?
questions.explanation: Guessing against stolen hashes on the attacker's own system is an offline attack, so it never touches the login service or its logs. An online brute force attack would generate failed logins and possibly lockouts.

questions.stem: Why do attackers often use password spraying instead of traditional brute force against online accounts?
choices: To reuse a captured session token
To stay under account lockout thresholds
To bypass encryption on the network
To crack stolen hashes faster offline
questions.answer: To stay under account lockout thresholds
questions.explanation: Trying one or two common passwords across many accounts keeps each account below the lockout limit. Cracking stolen hashes offline is a different attack that does not interact with live accounts.

questions.stem: Dozens of users across several departments were locked out within the same ten minutes. Logs show about 30 failed attempts against each of those accounts from one external address. Which of the following attacks is MOST likely?
questions.explanation: Many guesses against each account until it locks is a brute force attack. Password spraying uses only a few attempts per account specifically to avoid the lockouts seen here.

questions.stem: A server normally writes logs only during its nightly batch job. An analyst finds large new log entries written at 3:15 PM on a Sunday when no jobs were scheduled. Which of the following indicators does this BEST describe?
questions.explanation: Log activity at a time when the system normally writes nothing is out-of-cycle logging and may mean someone is using the system. Missing logs would be a gap in records, not unexpected extra entries.

questions.stem: A web server's CPU has been near 100% for three days and its outbound traffic has tripled, although the number of website visitors has not changed. Which of the following indicators does this BEST describe?
questions.explanation: Unexplained high CPU and network use points to unwanted activity such as cryptomining or data exfiltration. Resource inaccessibility would mean users could not reach the server or its data.

questions.stem: A security researcher posts on a public forum that a company's customer database is for sale and includes a sample containing real customer records. Which of the following indicators does this BEST describe?
questions.explanation: Evidence of a breach that has been posted or reported publicly is a published/documented indicator. The company's own logs played no part in this discovery, so the log-related options do not fit.

questions.stem: A workstation can no longer reach its antivirus vendor's update site or the operating system's patch servers, though every other website loads normally. Someone recently edited the workstation's hosts file. Which of the following indicators does this BEST describe?
questions.explanation: Malware often blocks security updates so it cannot be detected or removed, which shows up as blocked content. Nothing suggests high CPU or network use, so resource consumption does not fit.

questions.stem: A hospital moves its infusion pumps to their own VLAN, with firewall rules that let only the pump management server talk to them. Which of the following mitigation techniques is being used?
questions.explanation: Dividing the network into zones with controlled traffic between them is segmentation. Isolation would cut the pumps off from all other systems, but the management server can still reach them.

questions.stem: A water utility keeps the engineering workstation that programs its safety controllers completely disconnected from every other network. Data is moved to it only on approved, scanned media. Which of the following mitigation techniques does this BEST describe?
questions.explanation: Removing all network connections so a system cannot communicate with anything else is isolation, often called an air gap. Segmentation still allows controlled traffic between zones.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the main security benefit of network segmentation?
choices: It limits how far an attacker can move after a compromise
It encrypts all traffic between every host
It stops users from choosing weak passwords
It removes the need to patch the systems inside each network segment
questions.answer: It limits how far an attacker can move after a compromise
questions.explanation: Segmentation restricts which systems can reach each other, which contains lateral movement after a breach. It does not encrypt traffic or replace patching.

questions.stem: An audit finds that a file share containing HR records can be read by the Everyone group. Which of the following mitigations BEST addresses this finding?
choices: Restricting share permissions to the HR group
Installing a host-based firewall on the server
Enabling full-disk encryption on the server
questions.answer: Restricting share permissions to the HR group
questions.explanation: Changing permissions so only HR staff can read the files directly fixes the excessive access. Full-disk encryption protects a stolen drive but does nothing to stop logged-in users from reading the share.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST explains why an application allow list is more effective than a block list against brand-new malware?
choices: It scans files faster than antivirus software
Anything not approved in advance is blocked by default
It encrypts every program before it runs
questions.answer: Anything not approved in advance is blocked by default
questions.explanation: An allow list permits only known, approved programs, so new malware that no one has seen is still blocked. A block list stops only what has already been identified as bad.

questions.stem: A web application connects to its database using the database's built-in administrator account, even though it only needs to read and add rows in two tables. Which of the following mitigation techniques should be applied?
questions.explanation: Giving the application an account with only the rights it needs limits the damage if the application is compromised. Segmentation controls network paths, not the permissions an account has inside the database.

questions.stem: Monthly scans show the same missing operating system updates on hundreds of laptops because users keep postponing restarts. Which of the following would BEST address this?
choices: Moving the laptops to an isolated network
Automated patch deployment with a forced restart deadline
Adding every laptop to a strict application allow list policy
questions.answer: Automated patch deployment with a forced restart deadline
questions.explanation: Automating patching with a firm restart deadline makes sure updates are actually applied. An allow list controls which programs run but does not fix missing operating system patches.

questions.stem: Administrators often turn on an insecure legacy protocol on servers while troubleshooting and forget to turn it off again. Which of the following mitigation techniques would BEST make sure the setting does not stay enabled?
questions.explanation: Configuration enforcement keeps checking systems against the approved baseline and resets settings that drift. Patching fixes software flaws, but it does not undo a setting an administrator changed.

questions.stem: A company retired a web application but left its DNS record pointing to a cloud address it no longer owned. An attacker claimed that address and hosted a phishing page under the company's subdomain. Which of the following processes was done poorly?
questions.explanation: Proper decommissioning removes every trace of a retired system, including DNS records, so nothing is left for attackers to take over. There was no software flaw to patch; the problem was a leftover record.

questions.stem: The security team wants a tool on every laptop that records process, file and network activity, lets analysts investigate remotely and can cut a laptop off from the network with one click. Which of the following BEST meets these requirements?
questions.explanation: Endpoint detection and response records detailed activity, supports remote investigation and can contain a device. A HIPS blocks suspicious behavior, but it does not provide the investigation and response features described.

questions.stem: Which of the following mitigations would BEST help a security team notice an attacker using valid stolen credentials at unusual hours?
questions.explanation: Monitoring and alerting on login activity can spot valid accounts being used at odd times or places. An allow list controls which programs run and would not notice a legitimate login.

questions.stem: A database server should accept connections only from two application servers, including blocking other hosts on its own subnet that never pass through the network firewall. Which of the following BEST meets this requirement?
questions.explanation: A host-based firewall filters traffic on the server itself, so it can block neighbors on the same subnet. Antivirus looks for malicious files and does not filter which hosts may connect.

questions.stem: A security engineer is choosing between a host-based intrusion detection system (HIDS) and a host-based intrusion prevention system (HIPS) for critical servers. Which of the following is the PRIMARY difference?
choices: A HIPS works only with encrypted network traffic
A HIPS checks only network traffic; a HIDS only files
A HIDS does not need any software on the server
A HIPS can block what it detects; a HIDS only alerts
questions.answer: A HIPS can block what it detects; a HIDS only alerts
questions.explanation: Both watch activity on the host, but only the prevention system can stop it automatically. Both are installed on the host, so the claim that a HIDS needs no software is false.

questions.stem: A hardening review finds that servers still accept Telnet and SMBv1 connections, although SSH and newer SMB versions are available and in use. Which of the following hardening steps is BEST?
choices: Moving the servers to an isolated network
questions.explanation: Turning off old protocols that are no longer needed removes known weaknesses without affecting users. Isolating the servers would cut off the services users rely on.

questions.stem: A company sends backup tapes to an offsite vault by courier. It wants to make sure the data cannot be read if a tape is lost on the way. Which of the following mitigations BEST meets this goal?
choices: Applying least privilege to backup operators
Disabling unused ports on the backup server
questions.explanation: Encryption keeps the data unreadable to anyone without the key, even if the tape is lost. Segmentation and least privilege protect systems on the network, not a tape in a courier's van.

questions.stem: A workstation security baseline requires removing preinstalled trial programs and unused browser plug-ins. Which of the following is the PRIMARY benefit of this step?
choices: It removes the need for patching
It encrypts the data on the drive
questions.explanation: Every installed program is code that could contain a flaw, so removing unneeded software leaves fewer targets. Remaining software still needs patching, so this does not replace it.

questions.stem: Attackers learn that engineers at a defense contractor often read a small industry forum during lunch. They plant malicious code on that forum instead of emailing the engineers directly. Which of the following attack types does this describe?
questions.explanation: A watering hole attack compromises a site the target group already trusts and visits, then waits for them to arrive. Typosquatting is tempting because it also involves a website, but it relies on a look-alike domain that victims mistype, not on infecting a real site they use.
